title: `merge <pr> --ready` stops at a time limit and prints which step it waits on, instead of hanging silently
why: Finding (coordinator 13:46 CST Nov 14, from runner 10's logs ready3400.log and ready3400b.log; triage read none): `merge 3400 --ready` hung twice, 36 min and 11 min, after `ste-lint: PASS`. A python3 chain with a 600 s-old `sleep` child sat under it; no output, no timeout. Other PRs get the next line within 3 s. Debt candidate named by runner 10: the ready step has no timeout and prints nothing while a step waits, so a hang reads as slowness. Cost: 47 min of the runner's turn, n=1 PR, 2 runs. Cause on #3400 unknown; its lane is reproducing the single step now and was told not to run --ready. Not an owner question yet. Kin: merge-tool-beats-every-phase (a timed progress line per phase; its phase beat merged in #3404), stall-watch-ends-quiet-jobs, ready-checks-job-qualified-steps. First act of a lane: read what runs after `ste-lint` in `--ready`, reproduce the hang, then red then green: a `--ready` step that waits longer than its limit stops and names the step, and every step prints a line within a stated time. Check change: if a verdict moves, round 3 applies.
